config.title: Build slow query and slow route profiler hooks

intro.title: Build slow query and slow route profiler hooks
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js application that uses hooks to monitor and log slow database queries and slow API routes. You'll learn the core concept of middleware and event hooks to intercept and measure execution time. The main technologies involved are Node.js's built-in modules for timing and the Express.js framework for handling routes. By the end, you'll understand how to profile performance issues in a web server to identify bottlenecks.
intro.usecase: In production web applications, monitoring performance is critical for user experience and system health. This pattern is used in observability dashboards, like those in Datadog or New Relic, where developers track slow API endpoints and database queries to identify bottlenecks. For example, an admin panel might display a real-time table of slow routes, allowing engineers to quickly pinpoint and optimize problematic endpoints. Implementing these hooks enables proactive performance tuning, preventing degraded service during high traffic.

objectives: Implement a middleware function to capture route execution time
Configure threshold values to identify slow routes in a Node.js application
Construct a database query wrapper to measure query execution duration
Integrate timing hooks with logging mechanisms to report performance data
Manipulate request and response objects to inject timing metadata
Initialize profiler hooks at application startup
Apply conditional logic to trigger alerts for slow operations
